note: Third edition. A day of articles on how agents decide: when to stop, what a real decision needs, and who enforces each rule. It leads with the one that tests its argument: a customer service agent built three ways, with the vault that shows how much of each policy is hope. Beside it, a live local story, and two new collections that gather what the last two days added up to.

lead.why: One mandate, three designs and a published vault: the behaviour-policy argument measured rather than asserted, down to which rules a model is only hoped to keep.

highlights.why: Seven dimensions, seven levels, and the line below which a decider carries liability rather than agency. Its own vault holds the scale.
A hospital IT outage nobody could check from home, kept as evidence in a vault while it was still happening.
When every agent mistake adds a rule, the rules become the problem. Mapped, with the way back to shipping.
Zoom into an agent's policy and you find the business: the rules the user interface used to enforce by omission.
